places.name: Lisboa
past: The lords built their castle on the hill above the town, where it could watch the roads for leagues.
Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 35% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
A great fire burned 24 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 92% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 81 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the northern side; 0 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 57 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.
A great fire burned 62 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Cacilhas
past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
10 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.
A great fire burned 9 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
The ford was bridged in stone.
Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.
A great fire burned 17 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 9 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.

places.name: Marvila
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 85% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line; 2 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 15 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The Franciscans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 25 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 95% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 2 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the western side; 17 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 17 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
